name: Quality compounders
summary: High returns on capital, fat margins, steady growth and little debt.
how_to_read: Every filter must pass: ROIC of at least 15%, a gross margin of at least 40%, revenue growth of at least 8% a year over 3 years, an FCF margin of at least 10%, and net debt at most 2× EBITDA. A company with no net debt / EBITDA (for example, negative EBITDA or a sector where it's n/m) still passes that last test, so check the debt columns. Results are ranked by ROIC and FCF yield, half each. A high rank says nothing about price beyond the FCF yield.
misses: Asset-heavy businesses with naturally low gross margins.
Anything whose quality shows only over longer periods than these trailing numbers.
